entries.rootCause: The skill describes a broad localization workflow but does not tell agents to treat a project-supplied contract as the controlling closed specification, nor does it bundle a deterministic way to derive and validate contract-bound key parity and report output; consequently the observed agent guessed nonexistent directories, repeatedly reread files, and needed four ad hoc verification attempts before producing a passing check.
entries.reasoning: Evidence 0 is UNASSESSED rather than failing, so no quality defect is inferred. It nevertheless exposes a clear efficiency and contract-safety gap: the run had an exact v2 React contract, but the agent probed nonexistent src/components and src/pages, reread the same inputs many times, and wrote three faulty PowerShell checks before the fourth passed. The candidate therefore tightens the existing analysis and completeness steps in place and adds a bounded Node command for the source-established React/react-i18next v2 contract. The command delegates consecutive mechanical steps—read the contract and declared sources, extract confirmed data-i18n-key values, check corresponding t() calls and locale key parity, serialize the declared report, then validate its closed ABI—while translation meaning, interpolation correctness, framework initialization, and proof that protected bytes were unchanged remain agent duties. Expected score impact is primarily reduced tool churn and fewer schema/report mistakes; the evidence has no score, so this is not claimed as a demonstrated quality increase. Pre-edit checklist: (a) Generality: another React localization task with different source paths, locale names, keys, and report path under the same public v2 contract benefits because all such values are read from argv and contract fields, not hard-coded. (b) Rewrite-in-place: contract precedence and executable verification were inserted into the existing project-analysis and completeness-check sections rather than appended as overlapping policy. (c) Coherent scope: one dependency-free script covers only the independently supported v2 React boundary and leaves the skill's other frameworks on the original workflow. (d) No-trade-off: PER_TASK_SUMMARY contains no PASSING tasks, so there is no passing contract to regress; the sole UNASSESSED task's broad capability is preserved because the command is explicitly conditional and semantic work remains with the agent. Local validation used the digest-bound contract plus observed App/config/locale files, generated a report with the observed key set and zero missing keys, and exited successfully. The observed report is used only as a fidelity reference, not as proof of translation correctness.
